message.content: 獅子（屬於貓科）和斑馬（屬於馬科）雖然在現代分類上分屬不同的科，但它們都屬於哺乳綱中的偶蹄目（Perissodactyla）或鴨嘴獸目（Carnivora）? Wait, lions belong to Carnivora, zebras to Perissodactyla. Actually lions are in order Carnivora (Felidae), zebras in order Perissodactyla (Equidae). So they diverged earlier. Their most recent common ancestor would be a mammalian ancestor from the early Eocene (~50–60 million years ago) that gave rise to both the carnivore lineage leading to felids and the perissodactyl lineage leading to equids. This ancestor was likely a small, omnivorous, forest-dwelling mammal that lived during the Paleogene period. It was part of the larger clade called Laurasiatheria, which includes many modern land mammals such as ungulates, carnivores, bats, and cetartiodactyls. Thus, the common ancestor of lions and zebras was a primitive Laurasiatherian mammal from the early Eocene, before the split into distinct carnivore and odd-toed ungulate lineages.
